# Chicago Education Digest
_Jul 20 – Aug 03, 2026_

> Covering: K-12 Education & Schools · Board of Education & Governance

## K-12 Education & Schools

Chicago Public Schools' budget for the upcoming year was a central focus over the past two weeks, culminating in the Chicago Board of Education's approval of an amended $10 billion spending plan. This amended budget notably reversed earlier plans for staff furloughs, partly by reallocating $85 million in tax increment financing (TIF) dollars. However, the budget's passage relies on an anticipated $150 million in additional state funding, which has been committed to by Illinois House Speaker Welch but is not yet secured, raising concerns among some board members and stakeholders about the district's financial stability. While the amended budget aimed to mitigate some initial layoff plans, reports indicate that overall staffing cuts are still present, with specific impacts noted on Latino high schools, and Milwaukee Public Schools actively recruiting CPS teachers.

The budget discussions unfolded amidst a reported $700 million shortfall, partly attributed to issues with Cook County property tax collections. Concerns about the long-term financial health of the district and the governance process surrounding the budget's passage were voiced by some stakeholders. Beyond the budget, Chicago Public Schools announced plans to expand its Whole School Safety Model citywide. Separately, lunchroom workers have moved closer to a strike, and the Chicago Teachers Union, along with the Illinois Federation of Teachers, filed a lawsuit concerning property tax funds.

## Board of Education & Governance

The Chicago Board of Education recently approved an amended $10 billion budget for Chicago Public Schools. A central feature of this revised spending plan is its reliance on an additional $150 million in state funding that has not yet been formally appropriated by the Illinois General Assembly. This amended budget aims to reverse earlier proposals for over 1,700 teacher layoffs and eliminate planned furlough days. Prior to the amendment, concerns were raised about the impact of initial cuts, particularly on Latino high schools, and reports indicated that Milwaukee Public Schools was actively recruiting laid-off CPS teachers.

The Board's decision to pass a budget contingent on unconfirmed state funds drew criticism from some members and external observers, who questioned the financial prudence and "good governance" of the approach. While Illinois House Speaker Emanuel "Chris" Welch has publicly committed to securing the additional funding, its approval remains uncertain. This situation highlights ongoing concerns about CPS's financial stability, including a reported $700 million budget gap and challenges related to property tax collection. Discussions also touched upon the broader governance landscape, with mentions of challenges facing candidates for the upcoming elected school board.
